newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Excerpts from Kofi Annan's speech to UN Assembly.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from Kofi Annan's speech to UN Assembly.

text.p: Following are excerpts from a speech to the General Assembly by Kofi Annan of Ghana, the new U.N. secretary-general after he took the oath of office. He begins his five-year term on January 1.

"I wish to pay tribute to the vision and energy of Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, an extraordinary statesman who led the United Nations through a turbulent period of transition from the Cold War to a new, still emerging, era...(Turning to former Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar, he said, "Welcome home sir.")

"The time to choose is now. For this organisation, along with the rest of the world, must change. Let every member states welcome this change, not resist it. Let us make change our ally, not our enemy, seize it as an opportunity, not a threat, recognise it as a necessity, not an imposition..."

"If all of us in this hall together, with the participation of all nations, large and small, East and West, North and South, can make this organisation leaner, more efficient and more effective, more responsive to the wishes and needs of its members and more realistic in its goals and commitments, then and only then will we serve both this organisation's high purpose and the planet's best interests.

"All the old problems -- particularly peace and security amongst nations and social justice for their peoples -- still confront us...The world is beginning to recognise the many roots of conflict, the economic base of stability, and the grim truth that intolerance, injustice and oppression -- and their consequences -- respect no national frontiers.

"Similarly we now know that more than ever sustainable economic development is not merely a matter of projects and statistics. It is above all a matter of people -- real people with basic needs: food, clothing, shelter and medical care.
"Let us ensure that the voice of the United Nations in economic matters is heard by those members states with the greatest capacity to give..."

"In that spirit, let us embark on a time of healing: a healing of fractures and frictions between member states and this organisation, which cannot function without their political and material support; and a healing of wounded morale and ideals within the secretariat, whose dedicated staff deserve our thanks and encouragement.

"To the nations and peoples of the world whose representatives are assembled here today, I say simply this: the United Nations is your instrument for peace and justice. Use it; defend it. It can be no wiser, no more competent and more efficient than those member states that now comprise and guide it...

"Applaud us when we prevail; correct us when we fail; but, above all, do not let this indispensable, irreplaceable institution wither, languish or perish as a result of member state indifference, inattention or financial starvation...
"Alone I can do nothing. Together, we can irreversibly advance the frontiers of peace, dignity and justice for all humankind."
